game: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Nintendo Switch 2 remake)

findings.name: Gold Skulltula Tokens
findings.detail: 100 total (56 overworld / 44 dungeon per KeenGamer). Most in original positions; 5 changes: Zora's River token moved from tree to soft soil by Magic Bean Salesman; Lake Hylia island-monument token moved to SW crawlspace (no longer night-only); Lon Lon Ranch 4->3 and Hyrule Field +1 (lone east tree); Water Temple bombable-wall token now Bombs not Longshot; Deku Tree Gohma Larva room token reached by burning web + Slingshot. Each dies in 1 hit.
findings.trackable: Map screen shows per-region Gold Skulltula count found (KeenGamer, games.gg). No confirmed global running total.

findings.name: House of Skulltula rewards
findings.detail: 10: Adult's Wallet (500 rupees); 20: Echo Gem (replaces Stone/Shard of Agony); 30: Giant's Wallet (1,000); 40: Bombchus (20 per KeenGamer); 50: Piece of Heart; 100: Gold Rupee (200 rupees, repeatable per KeenGamer).
findings.trackable: Token count at House of Skulltula / token counter (not independently confirmed in remake)

findings.name: Pieces of Heart
findings.detail: 36 total, same as original, excluding 8 boss Heart Containers (games.gg; finalboss.io says 20 hearts total = 3 + 8 + 9). Some moved: Business Scrub piece moved to a grotto near Hyrule Castle Town (needs Fairy Thought password); Lon Lon Ranch grotto piece moved to a magically locked chest near Gerudo Valley road (interact child, adult, child). Sources CONFLICT on Ice Cavern piece: games.gg says gone / new pieces in Hyrule Field and Death Mountain Crater; another summary says moved to Death Mountain Crater. Hyrule Field Business Scrub reportedly 100 rupees vs 10.
findings.trackable: Map shows how many Heart Pieces remain per region (games.gg); Zelda Wiki-derived article says map shows collectible status per area.

findings.name: Echo Gem
findings.detail: NEW. Replaces Stone/Shard of Agony; earned at 20 tokens; must be equipped; light and sound cue for nearby Gold Skulltulas (trees, crates, soil, Secret Grottos).

findings.name: Bottles
findings.detail: 5 slots (was 4 in N64); fifth bottle from the Potion Shop in Hyrule Castle Town. Poe Collector bottle requires 5 Big Poes (per Zelda Wiki-cited article); 10 Big Poes earns Gold Rupee.
findings.trackable: Poe Collector point counter (unconfirmed in remake)

findings.name: Business Scrub Seed
findings.detail: NEW consumable; summons a Deku merchant where thrown. Found in new chests and from amiibo.

findings.name: Fairy Thoughts
findings.detail: NEW spots offering advice; can drop items/restore hearts; one gives a password to a Business Scrub.

findings.name: Wallets
findings.detail: Child wallet starts at 200 (per Nintendo Everything), Adult 500, Giant 1,000 (Gold Skulltula rewards). Quiver max 50, Bomb Bag 40, Bullet Bag 50, Sticks 30, Nuts 40 (finalboss.io, original values; unconfirmed for remake).

findings.name: Great Fairy gifts
findings.detail: Collection screen shows Gift of Improved Spin, Gift of Doubled Magic, Gift of Halved Damage (3 Great Fairies in remake per Zelda Wiki-cited article). finalboss.io lists 6 fairy rewards (original-game structure), so remake count unconfirmed.
findings.trackable: Collection screen (Quest Status split into Collection and Key Item menus)

findings.name: Silver Rupees removed
findings.detail: Replaced by silver gems that fly into door-lock slots.

findings.name: Gerudo Proving Grounds
findings.detail: Gerudo Training Ground renamed; 30 rupee attempt (was 10), on path to Horseback Archery Range.

findings.name: Original side content assumed present
findings.detail: Trading sequence/Biggoron sword, Happy Mask Shop (Mask of Truth), Big Poes (10), fishing, shooting galleries, Horseback archery, Bombchu Bowling, Treasure Chest Game, Dampe, frogs, Epona/Malon. finalboss.io lists them but only as original structure; remake-specific changes not verified.

findings.name: Hall of Fallen Foes
findings.detail: Enemy museum with boss rematches / boss rush; part of Zelda Notes features list (Nintendo Everything). Whether it is in-console or phone-only is unclear (one review says in-game).

findings.name: amiibo support
findings.detail: Support for all Zelda amiibo, which give helpful items.

findings.name: Zelda Notes (NSO)
findings.detail: Features: Access Map, Gossip Quests (photo/location points exchanged for ocarina scores), Hall of Fallen Foes, Today's Record (stats incl. enemies defeated), My Play Data, Global Play Data, Photo Studio, Threads of Time, amiibo, Play Ocarina, OoT Quiz (2000+ questions, 1/day). Reported locked behind Nintendo Switch Online and smart device — not trophy-suitable.

trackableStats.stat: Gold Skulltulas / Heart Pieces found per region
trackableStats.where: Map screen; remaining count shown on world map
Story log only; main progression, NOT a completion tracker per Zelda Dungeon summary
Quest Status split into Collection and Key Item menus

versionNotes.note: Remake is Switch 2 exclusive; Zelda Notes features need NSO and a smart device.
Remake: 5 bottles (N64 4), Echo Gem replaces Stone of Agony, Silver Rupees replaced, 5 Skulltula relocations, several Heart Piece relocations.

gaps: Zelda Wiki and Zelda Dungeon returned 403; I could not read the primary Zelda Wiki remake page, only articles claiming to cite it. No Nintendo official page checked.
Many sources are SEO/guide sites of unknown reliability; no source explicitly stated a global running total of Skulltulas/Heart Pieces on-screen.
Conflict: Ice Cavern Heart Piece 'moved to Death Mountain Crater' vs 'gone, new pieces in Hyrule Field and Crater'. Also the 36 total is stated but per-piece list not verified.
Heart Containers: 8 boss assumed from original; Great Fairy count, Big Poe count/reward thresholds, Biggoron trading chain, mask quest, minigame changes unverified for remake.
DLC/paid extras: none found; no source mentions any (Master Quest not confirmed or denied).
Post-game content other than Hall of Fallen Foes not found.
Songs count and Magic Bean count not verified for remake (finalboss.io says 12 songs and 10 beans, original-based).
Does the game track total enemies defeated / Big Poes / fish records: unconfirmed (Today's Record is Zelda Notes only).
